chunks.title: Ismael
chunks.text:
C1. [CORPUS] "Frou" / "Froue" = Frau/Frauen ("vo syre erschte Frou"; "zwüsche dene beidne Froue"). Bernese harvest: Frou 1, Froue 2, Frau 0. The Zürich harvest contains neither form; Zürich "Frau" occurs only in als.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enge (comparison, not harvested). Bernese drops the -w- in the plural - record as Bernese-attested.
C2. [CORPUS] "geit" = geht, twice ("geit är uf dä Vorschlag y"; "So geit d Hagar zrügg u bringt der Ismael uf d Wält"). Bernese harvest geit 3; Zürich harvest geit 0. See Brauerei C3 for why the Zürich side is only in-corpus for the absence.
C3. [CORPUS] "zwöi" = zwei ("Im Kapitel 17 chöme die zwöi e neue Name"). See Bauern-Tabak C4 - clean Bern "zwöi" vs Zürich "zwei" opposition, both sides in-corpus.
C4. [CORPUS] "Är" = er (3sg masculine pronoun) - "Är isch der erschti Sohn", "Är tuet das nur wil", "Är het ds Gebiet". The Zürich harvest uses plain "er" ("Er wird je nach Land diräkt vo de Bürger ... gwählt", "Er vertritt d Gmeind au nach usse"). Bernese vs Zürich opposition, both in-corpus. Basel side not attested.
C5. [CORPUS] "nid" for "nicht", four times. See the Basel comparison C-notes in Ausländer C1 - this is the strongest lexical Basel/Bern vs Zürich opposition in the harvest.
C6. [CORPUS] "Jahr" ("10 Jahr") vs Basel "Joor". See Bauern-Tabak C5.
C7. [CORPUS] "tuet" = tut ("Är tuet das nur wil är druuf vertrout"). The Zürich harvest contains no verb of the "tun" class, so the Zürich counterpart ("z tue", Enge/Bünzli) is comparison-only.
C8. [UNVERIFIED] "Wüschti Schur", "Pharan", "Beerscheba" - Biblical landscape lexicon with no attested

chunks.title: Kaffeeratte
chunks.text:
"D Kaffiratte (Golunda ellioti) isch e Nager, wo z Südasie verbreitet isch u dert mal als Kaffischädling isch gfürchtet gsi."
"D Ratte het e Chopfrumpflengi zwüschen 11 u 15 Zentimeter."
"Der Schwanz isch zwüsche 9 u 13 Zentimeter läng."
"Es git graui, bruuni, gälbbruuni u rotbruuni Ratte."
"Einigi Exemplar erinnere mit ihrer Fällfarb an es Kaffigrem."
"Ou d Struktur vom Fälli isch je nach Region sehr underschidlech."
"Gwüssi Kaffiratte hei es relativ weichs, anderi es borstigs bis stachligs Fäll."
"D Kaffiratte het e breide Körberbou, genau so wi d Wüehlmuus."
"Ds Verbreitigsgebiet erstreckt sech vom üsserschten Oschte vom Iran über Pakischtan bis nach Indie."
"Ou Nepal u Sri Lanka ghöre derzue."
"Dört läbt d Kaffiratte i underschidleche Läbesrüüm wi di grasigi Steppe, d Sümpf u d Rägewälder."
"Si chöme aber ou am Rand vo Fälder u Plantasche vor."
"Obwohl si chöi chlättere, halte si sech meischtens uf em Boden uf."
"Bsunders guet vermehrt sech d Kaffiratten i der Neechi vo Kaffiplantasche."
"Dert frisst si d Chnoschpen u d Blüete vo der Kaffipflanze."
"Syt me der Kaffiabou z Sri Lanka ufgä het, het d Zahl vo de Kaffiratte wider abgno."
"Dert schynt si sech aber nid derart explosionsartig z vermehre wi denn z Sri Lanka."
"Z Indie gilt si nach wi vor als Kaffischädling."

chunks.title: Kaffeeratte
chunks.text:
S1. "Die Kaffiratte (Golunda ellioti) ist ein Nager, das in Südasien verbreitet ist und dort als Kaffeeschädling gefürchtet war."
S2. "Die Ratte hat eine Kopfrumpflänge zwischen 11 und 15 Zentimeter."
S3. "Der Schwanz ist zwischen 9 und 13 Zentimeter lang."
S4. "Es gibt graue, braune, gelbbraune und rotbraune Ratten."
S5. "Einige Exemplare erinnern mit ihrer Fellfarbe an einen Kaffee crem."
S6. "Auch die Struktur vom Fell ist je nach Region sehr unterschiedlich."
S7. "Gewisse Kaffiratten haben ein relativ weiches, andere ein borstiges bis stacheliges Fell."
S8. "Die Kaffiratte hat einen breiten Körperbau, genau so wie die Wühlmaus."
S9. "Das Verbreitungsgebiet erstreckt sich vom äussersten Osten vom Iran über Pakistan bis nach Indien."
S10. "Auch Nepal und Sri Lanka gehören dazu."
S11. "Dort lebt die Kaffiratte in unterschiedlichen Lebensräumen wie die grasige Steppe, die Sümpfe und die Regenwälder."
S12. "Sie kommt aber auch am Rand von Feldern und Plantagen vor."
S13. "Obwohl sie klettern können, halten sie sich meistens auf dem Boden auf."
S14. "Besonders gut vermehrt sich die Kaffiratte im Schatten von Kaffeepflanzen."
S15. "Dort frisst sie die Knospen und die Blüten von der Kaffeepflanze."
S16. "Seit der Kaffeeanbau in Sri Lanka zunahm, hat die Zahl der Kaffiratten wieder abgenommen."
S17. "Dort scheint sie sich aber nicht so explosionsartig zu vermehren wie damals in Sri Lanka."
S18. "In Indien gilt sie nach wie vor als Kaffeeschädling."

chunks.title: Kaffeeratte
chunks.text:
C1. [CORPUS] "wi" = wie/as, three times in the sentence list ("genau so wi d Wüehlmuus"; "Läbesrüüm wi di grasigi Steppe"; "nach wi vor"). The Zürich harvest contains no "wi" token, but nor does it contain an alternative in this slot, so no substitution can be evidenced. Recorded as Bernese-attested only.
C2. [CORPUS] "gwüssi" = gewisse. Zürich shows the same prefix ("Es sind öppe 230'000...", "gwüssi alkaholfrei Erfrüschigsgetränk"), so SHARED, not a marker. Recorded to prevent a false positive.
C3. [CORPUS] "underschidlech" = unterschiedlich. Zürich uses the same ch-digraph ("underschiidlechei", "underschidlechem"), so SHARED.
C4. [CORPUS] "het" = hat (3sg). Basel, Bern and Zürich all use unprefixed "het". NOT a discriminator; recorded to prevent a false positive.
C5. [CORPUS] "chöme/chöi" = können, with k- spelled ch-. Zürich uses the same ("chönne Bier i gueter Qualität lifere"). SHARED.
C6. [CORPUS] "wider" = wieder. Zürich uses "wider" too ("wider iigfüehrt worde", "wider ufbout"). SHARED.
C7. [UNVERIFIED] "Südasie", "Indie" - the final-n deletion in "Indien". No Basel or Zürich cognate was found in my sample, so no cross-dialect claim is made.
C8. IMPORTANT NEGATIVE FINDING: this article contains NO lexeme that contrasts with Basel. It is included as clean, long, unambiguously Bernese everyday prose, not as dialect-contrast material. Do not build contrast items from it.

chunks.title: Mattenenglisch
chunks.text:
"Ds Mattenänglisch isch e Soziolekt vom Bärndütsche."
"Die mattenänglischi Gheimsprach glycht em Pig Latin, wo im änglische Sprachruum verbreitet isch."
"Es zeichnet sech aber bsunders derdür uus, das der erscht Vokal immer ganz ersetzt wird."
"Teil Lüt bezeichne nume die Gheimsprach als Mattenänglisch."
"Der mattenänglisch Soziolekt het e Huuffe spezielli Usdrück gha."
"Es git aber e Verein, wo's bis hüt pflegt."
"Hindedra chunt es ee, u der erscht Vokal wird ersetzt dür nes i."

chunks.title: Mattenenglisch
chunks.text:
S1. "Das Mattenänglisch ist ein Soziolekt des Berndeutschen."
S2. "Die mattenänglische Geheimsprache gleicht dem Pig Latin, das im englischen Sprachraum verbreitet ist."
S3. "Sie zeichnet sich aber besonders dadurch aus, dass der erste Vokal immer ganz ersetzt wird."
S4. "Teile Leute bezeichnen die Geheimsprache lediglich als Mattenänglisch."
S5. "Der mattenänglische Soziolekt hat eine Fülle spezieller Ausdrücke gehabt."
S6. "Es gibt aber einen Verein, der ihn bis heute pflegt."
S7. "Hinterher kommt ein ee, und der erste Vokal wird durch ein i ersetzt."

chunks.title: Mattenenglisch
chunks.text:
C1. [CORPUS] "bbruucht" / "bbruucht" shows gemination of b before /r/. The source sentence is too long to quote whole (23 words) so it is NOT in the sentence list; it reads: "Syt sech im Louff vom 20igschte Jahrhundert d Bevölkerigsstruktur vo däm Quartier starch het veränderet, wird ds Mattenänglischen im Alltag nümm bbruucht." The same article also has the non-geminated variant "wird hüt zwar nümm bbrucht". Basel [COMPARISON] writes plain "bruucht" (e.g. als.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basel-Altstadt_(Grossbasel): "...Reformazion]] ziitwiis as Lager bruucht..."). NOTE the register split INSIDE Bernese: geminate bb- in colloquial narrative prose, plain b- in the more formal lexicographic register. Do not treat gemination as categorical.
C2. [COMPARISON] "z tüe" (Bernese "tun") vs Zürich "z tue". Bernese occurrence is in this article ("Sy Name het nüt mit Änglisch z tüe, sondern mit sym Ursprungsort..." - sentence too long to quote whole). Zürich "z tue" is attested in als.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bünzli ("hät mit öisem Bünzli nüüt z tue") and /Enge ("händ die früene Mäntschen äinewääg nüüt z tue") - both fetched for comparison, NEITHER is part of this harvest. Basel side never observed; make no Basel claim.
C3. [CORPUS] "erscht" for "erst" appears twice in this article's sentence list ("der erscht Vokal"). Bernese corpus total: erscht 2, eerschtu 0. Contrast with Wallisertiitsch "eerschtu" (2, zero "erscht") - see the Ayent file, C6. This is a usable minimal-pair final-devoicing item.
C4. [CORPUS] "Hindedra chunt es ee, u der erscht Vokal wird ersetzt dür nes i." - verb-final order after

chunks.title: Mattenenglisch
chunks.text: C8. LEXICON MOVED OUT OF THE SENTENCE LIST: this article's glossary items "Jiu 'ja'", "Gieu (Giel) 'Bueb'", "Modi 'Meitschi'", "Chemp 'Stei'" are 2-3 words each and therefore violate the 6-20 word sentence rule. They are the most dialectal material in the article and are recorded here instead. Use them as vocabulary items, not as sentences.

chunks.title: Ayent
chunks.text:
"Zer Gmei Ayent gcheerunt di Deerfer Botyre, Luc, Saxonne, La Place, Blignou, Fortunau, Saint-Romain, Signèse, Villa, Argnou und Anzère."
"Im Noordu geit ds Gmeigibiet bis uf ds Wildhooru emüf."
"Dur ds Taal vaner Lienne fiert der Füesswäg zum Rawilpass."
"Ayent isch zum eerschtu Mal im Jaar 1052 als Agent (1250 als Argenta) erwäänts cho."
"Dr Gmeipresidänt va Ayent isch dr Marco Aymon (Stand Oktoober 2017)."
"Dr tradizionell Dialäkt va Ayent gcheert zum Frankoprovenzalischu."

chunks.title: Ayent
chunks.text:
S1. "Zur Gemeinde Ayent gehören die Dörfer Botyre, Luc, Saxonne, La Place, Blignou, Fortunau, Saint-Romain, Signèse, Villa, Argnou und Anzère."
S2. "Im Norden geht das Gemeindegebiet bis hinauf zum Wildhorn empor."
S3. "Durch das Tal der Lienne führt der Fussweg zum Rawilpass."
S4. "Ayent ist zum ersten Mal im Jahr 1052 als Agent erstmals erwähnt."
S5. "Der Gemeindepräsident von Ayent ist Marco Aymon (Stand Oktober 2017)."
S6. "Der traditionelle Dialekt von Ayent gehört zum Frankoprovenzalischen."

chunks.title: Ayent
chunks.text:
C1. [CORPUS] "vaner" / "vanu" = von, four times ("Im Taal vaner Lienne", "Dur ds Taal vaner Lienne", "98,2 % vanu Iwonru"). CONTRAST [CORPUS]: exclusive to the Wallisertiitsch harvest; basel, bern, zurich and walser have zero. Bern/Zürich/Basel use "vo" (23 / 37 / 242), Walser uses "vù"/"vam". THE most exclusive lexical marker in the corpus.
C2. [CORPUS] "gcheerunt"/"gcheert" = gehören/gehört, four times ("Zer Gmei Ayent gcheerunt di Deerfer..."; "Dr tradizionell Dialäkt va Ayent gcheert zum Frankoprovenzalischu"). Attested ONLY in the Wallisertiitsch harvest; absent from basel, bern, zurich and walser.
C3. [CORPUS] "Gmei" = Gemeinde. THREE-WAY CONTRAST: Wallis "Gmei" 3 / "Gmeind" 0; Zürich "Gmeind" 6 / "Gmei" 0; Walser "Gmäind" 1. Basel unusable (infobox noise).
C4. [CORPUS] Final devoicing ABSENT in Wallisertiitsch: "eerschtu" (2 occurrences, "zum eerschtu Mal") against Bernese "erscht" (2). The two forms differ only in the ending, so they form a near-ideal minimal pair for a devoicing test item. Contrast with Basel and Walser, which both write the devoiced "Joor" (Basel 17, Walser 3) while Bernese and Zürich write "Jahr"/"Jaarhundert". This is the cleanest devoicing test in the corpus - and it confirms the brief's Basel devoicing while showing Bern/Zürich and Wallis sit on OPPOSITE sides of the line.
C5. [CORPUS] "deerfer" = Dörfer. Not attested in the other four corpora. Recorded as Wallisertiitsch-attested.
C6. [COMPARISON] "Füesswäg" = Fussweg contains the -wäg element that also appears in Bernese ("Wäg sym Gruch", "der Wäg afa äbne"). So "wäg" is NOT exclusively Bern

chunks.title: Blatten (Lötschen) (display title: Uf der Blattun / uf dr Blattun)
chunks.text:
"Uf dr Blattun, offiziell Blatten, isch en Gmei im Bizirk Weschtli Araro im Wallis."
"Ds Dorf liggut z obrusch im Leetschentaal."
"Dir ds Taal fliesst d Lonza, e Situfluss vam Rottu."
"Zer Gmei gcheerunt d Wiilra Eistn, Ried und Wiissuried."
"D Chilchu, wa anu 1985 gibüwwti cho ischt, het ds Patrozinium vaner Chinigi vam Roosuchranz."
"Obuna am Langgletscher steit am Bäärggraat über der Leetscherlicka, wa mu zum Aletschgletscher emubergeit d Hollandiahitta vam SAC."
"Uf dr Blattun ischt zum eerschtu Mal im Jaar 1433 als uffen der Blattun erwäänts cho."
"Ds Dorf uf der Blattun und dr Wiiler Ried sind Ändi Mai 2025 zum grossu Teil vama Bäärgsturz verschittuti cho."
"98,2 % vanu Iwonru sint im Jaar 2000 remisch-katholischi gsii."
"Der Gmeipresidänt uf der Blattun ischt dr Matthias Bellwald (Stand Mai 2025)."
"Bi der Volchszellig 2000 heint vanu 281 Iwonru 99,6 % Titsch als Höiptspraach agigää und 0,4 % anneri Spraache."
"Der heggschtalemannisch Dialäkt va Blattu gcheert ze weschtlichu Dialäktu vam Wallisertiitsch."

chunks.title: Blatten (Lötschen) (display title: Uf der Blattun / uf dr Blattun)
chunks.text:
S1. "Uf der Blattun, offiziell Blatten, ist eine Gemeinde im Bezirk Westlich Raron im Wallis."
S2. "Das Dorf liegt ganz oben im Lötschental."
S3. "Durch das Tal fliesst die Lonza, ein Seitenfluss der Rhone."
S4. "Zur Gemeinde gehören die Weiler Eistn, Ried und Weissuried."
S5. "Die Kirche, die 1985 eingeweiht wurde, hat das Patrozinium des Heiligen Franziskus vom Rosenkranz."
S6. "Ganz oben am Längsgletscher steht am Berggrat über der Lötschcherlücke, wo man zum Aletschgletscher hinübergeht, die Hollandiahütte des SAC."
S7. "Uf der Blattun ist zum ersten Mal im Jahr 1433 als uffen der Blattun erstmals erwähnt."
S8. "Das Dorf Uf der Blattun und der Weiler Ried sind Ende Mai 2025 zum grössten Teil vom Bergsturz verschüttet."
S9. "98,2 % von 281 Einwohnern waren im Jahr 2000 römisch-katholisch."
S10. "Der Gemeindepräsident Uf der Blattun ist Matthias Bellwald (Stand Mai 2025)."
S11. "Bei der Volkszählung 2000 haben von 281 Einwohnern 99,6 % Deutsch als Hauptsprache angegeben und 0,4 % eine andere Sprache."
S12. "Der höchstalemannische Dialekt von Blatten gehört zum westlichen Teil des Wallisertitsch."

chunks.title: Blatten (Lötschen) (display title: Uf der Blattun / uf dr Blattun)
chunks.text:
C1. [CORPUS] "ischt" for "ist", three times ("D Chilchu, wa anu 1985 gibüwwti cho ischt, het ds Patrozinium vaner Chinigi"; "Uf dr Blattun ischt zum eerschtu Mal im Jaar 1433"; "Der Gmeipresidänt uf der Blattun ischt dr Matthias Bellwald"). CONTRAST [CORPUS]: "ischt" occurs ONLY in the alpine dialects (walser 2, valais 3) and never in basel (156 "isch"), bern (24) or zurich (33). See Klosters C1.
C2. [CORPUS] "Gmei" = Gemeinde (monophthong), three times ("ischt en Gmei im Bizirk Weschtli Araro"; "Zer Gmei gcheerunt d Wiilra Eistn"). THREE-WAY CONTRAST: Wallis "Gmei" 3 / "Gmeind" 0; Zürich "Gmeind" 6 / "Gmei" 0; Walser "Gmäind". Basel is unusable for this item (its "Gmäind" occurrences are infobox noise).
C3. [CORPUS] "vaner"/"vanu" = von: "het ds Patrozinium vaner Chinigi". CONTRAST [CORPUS]: "vaner"/"vanu" occur only in the Wallisertiitsch harvest (vaner 2, vanu 2) and are absent from basel, bern, zurich and walser, all of which use "vo" (Basel 242, Bern 23, Zürich 37). Walser instead uses "vù"/"vam" (8). This is the most exclusive lexical marker in the whole corpus.

C5. [CORPUS] "mu" = man, in "wa mu zum Aletschgletscher emubergeit". THREE-WAY: Wallis "mu" 1; Zürich "mer" 5 and "me" 2; Bern "me"/"Me" 4; Basel "me" 8. Clean.

chunks.title: Issime (display title: Éischeme)
chunks.text:
S1. "Wegen dem ist Éischeme über ein paar Jahrhunderte zweisprachig gewesen."
S2. "Der Gründer des Hauses Savoyen, Humbert I. mit dem weissen Handschuh, erhielt im Jahr 1025 das Aostatal vom Lehen."

chunks.title: Issime (display title: Éischeme)
chunks.text:
C1. [CORPUS] "ischt" for "ist" is the dominant form in this article ("Z Éischeme isch scho ane 1184 e aigeschdändigi Chilchegmai belaid", "Goabi isch ane 1786 e aigeschdändigi Chilchegmai woore"). CONTRAST [CORPUS]: "ischt" occurs ONLY in the alpine dialects in the whole harvest (walser 2, valais 3) and is entirely absent from basel (156 "isch"), bern (24) and zurich (33). See Klosters C1 - this CORRECTS the brief's hypothesis that devoicing is a Basel-vs-Zürich split.
C2. [CORPUS] This article self-documents its own phonology with attested examples, which makes it the single most valuable Walser item for a dialect benchmark. Documented rules: (a) full old-Germanic vowels survive in unstressed syllables - "machu" (dt. machen); (b) mhd. -rn > -re - "Huore" (dt. Horn); (c) mhd. -nk > -nch - "tringche" (dt. trinken); (d) mhd. -hs > -ks - "Fuks" (dt. Fuchs); (e) German s > sch - "dschi" (dt. sie), "ünsch" (dt. uns); (f) mhd. long vowels diphthongised - "Hous" (dt. Haus), "Vöir" (dt. Feuer), "Eisch" (dt. Eis), "Oabe" (dt. Abend), "Chiesch" (dt. Käse); (g) mhd. diphthongs monophthongised - "Diib" (dt. Dieb), "Güüti" (dt. Güte), "Bruuder" (dt. Bruder); (h) mhd. a and ë broken to oa / ea before liquids - "oalt" (dt. alt), "geärbe" (dt. gerben).
C3. [CORPUS] The article contains an explicit in-dialect comparison with Wallisertiitsch: "Im Geegesaz zue dr andere Südwalserdialäkt und zuem Walliserdytsch sin mhd. ü, ö, üe in dr Éischemtöitschu nid endrùnded: Möisch (dt. chunks.title: Klosters (display title: Bim Chlooschtär oder Chlooschtärsch)
chunks.text:
"Di verschidänä Frakzionä vam Chlooschtär sind alles Walsersidligä."
"Dr Namä gäid uf di Prämonschtratenserpropstii am Platz bin dr Chilchä St. Jakob zrugg."
"Diä Abchleerigä sind duä aber wirräm abgäbrochä chon."
"Di Gmäind Chlooschtärsch ischt mit dr Rhätischä Bahn guet ärschlossän."
"Än nüüwä Baahof heds bim Dörfji und häjinnä am Platz."

This is the cleanest devoicing contrast available and it runs Alps-vs-low-Alemannic, not Basel-vs-Zürich.

C1. [CORPUS] "Züri" = Zürich, also a shared endonym used by every dialect of this wiki (including the Bernese and Wallisertiitsch files, which write "Züri"/"Bärn" when naming cities). NOT a dialect discriminator. Recorded to prevent a false contrast.
C2. [CORPUS] "ghört zue de Seemundarte" - the preposition "zue" before consonants is shared with Bernese ("z Kanaan", "z Galiläa"). NOT a discriminator.
C3. [CORPUS] "gläge" = gelegen, the participle g- prefix. Bernese shows the same ("nümm bbruucht", "ufgnoh worde"). SHARED morphology, not a marker.
C4. [UNVERIFIED] "Buebike", "Buobinger", "liit", "Bucke" vowel forms are Zürcher Oberland / Seemundart vocabulary with no attested Basel or Bern cognate in my sample. No claim made.
C5. [CORPUS] "hüt" ("is hüt di am beste erhalteni") - SHARED with Basel and Bern. Recorded as a negative result: "hüt" is not Zürich-specific.
C6. SCOPE LIMIT: this article's distinctive material is lexical (place names, -liit, the ue-diphthong), not grammatical. It contributes Seemundart vocabulary. Do NOT use it as evidence for Zürich-vs-Basel GRAMMATICAL contrasts - the city-Zürich articles (Bürgermeister, Ausländer) are the correct source for those.

C1. PROVENANCE: this is the CITY Zürich article (dialect tag "Züritüütsch" with no "(See)" qualifier), so it is the reference point for urban Zürich German, unlike Kloster Einsiedeln which is Seedialect.

chunks.title: Basler Fasnacht
chunks.text:
F1. The Basel Fasnacht is the largest carnival in Switzerland. — cross-ref: none
F2. The Basel Fasnacht lasts exactly 72 hours. — cross-ref: none
F3. The Basel Fasnacht is today regarded as the only large Protestant carnival in the world. — cross-ref: none
F4. The Fasnachts-Comité has organised the Basel Fasnacht since 1911. — cross-ref: none
F5. In Basel a 'Masgge' (mask) means a costumed figure — one that wears both a costume (Goschdyym) and a mask (Larve); the two words are not synonyms. — cross-ref: none
F6. The largest Fasnacht in the canton Basel-Landschaft is that of Liestal, drawing tens of thousands of spectators. — cross-ref: none
F7. Over 12,000 participants are organised into groups, plus about 6,000 unregistered 'wild' Fasnächtler. — cross-ref: none
F8. The earliest mention of the Fasnacht is from 1376, the 'Böse Fasnacht'. — cross-ref: none
F9. In 1529 the carnival period was fixed to the three days from Monday to Wednesday after Ash Wednesday — the reason Basel Carnival falls a week later than elsewhere. — cross-ref: none
F10. At the 1540 muster, 600 young men in armour with sword and halberd marched through the city. — cross-ref: none
F11. The Fasnachts-Comité issues a badge in four metal grades: copper (9), silver (18), gold (45) and the 'Bijou' (about 100). — cross-ref: none

chunks.title: Bundesrat (Schweiz)
chunks.text:
F1. The Federal Council has exactly seven members; each member is individually called a Federal Councillor (Bundesrat/Bundesrätin). — cross-ref: S001
F2. Federal Councillors are elected by the United Federal Assembly for a four-year term. — cross-ref: S001
F3. The Federal Council is simultaneously the collective head of state of Switzerland. — cross-ref: S001
F4. The seven Federal Councillors govern collegially; each nonetheless heads one department (departmental principle, Departemäntalprinzip). — cross-ref: S001
F5. The President of the Confederation is 'primus inter pares', has no rights beyond the other Federal Councillors, and merely represents the country and chairs the Federal Council meeting. — cross-ref: S001
F6. The presidency passes through all Federal Councillors in order of seniority. — cross-ref: S001
F7. The Federal Chancellor supports the Federal Council in an advisory capacity and is distinct from the seven decision-makers. — cross-ref: S001
F8. The Federal Chancellery is the Federal Council's staff office (Stabsstelle). — cross-ref: S012b
F9. After their election the Federal Councillors allocate the federal departments among themselves; Parliament has formally no say in the allocation. — cross-ref: S001
F10. The principle of collegiality rests on unwritten tradition, not on statute. — cross-ref: S001

chunks.title: Bundesversammlung (Schweiz)
chunks.text:
F1. The Federal Assembly (Bundesversammlung) is the Swiss parliament, established by the Federal Constitution. — cross-ref: S002
F2. The Federal Assembly is the legislative branch of the state. — cross-ref: S006
F3. Parliamentary members are elected by the people every four years. — cross-ref: S002
F4. When the two chambers sit together they constitute the United Federal Assembly (Vereinigti Bundesversammlig), as happens for the Federal Council and Federal Supreme Court elections. — cross-ref: S002
F5. The President of the National Council chairs the United Federal Assembly and is therefore also styled 'der höchscht Schwiizer' — but this is purely honorific and ranks ninth in protocol. — cross-ref: S002
F6. Parliament elects the Federal Councillors, the President of the Confederation, the federal judges and the Federal Chancellor — and in the case of war, the general as supreme commander. — cross-ref: S002
F7. A person convicted by the Federal Supreme Court may lodge a pardon application, which is judged by the chambers. — cross-ref: S002
F8. The Federal Assembly has existed since the founding of the Swiss federal state in 1848. — cross-ref: S048
F9. Bern is called the 'Bundesstadt' (federal city) because the Federal Assembly sits there. — cross-ref: S002

chunks.title: Direkte Demokratie
chunks.text:
F1. "Direct democracy" (diräkti Demokratii, also "unmittelbare Demokratii") denotes both a procedure and a political system. — cross-ref: S004
F2. Direct democracy is distinguished from representative/indirect democracy, in which the people elect members of a council who then decide. — cross-ref: S006
F3. Combining elements of direct and indirect democracy yields the term "semi-direct" or "plebiscitary" democracy — the term standardly applied to the Swiss system. — cross-ref: S048
F4. The most immediate form of direct democracy is the Landsgemeinde, still existing in a few Swiss cantons, or at communal level the Gemeindeversammlung. — cross-ref: S040
F5. In Switzerland the semi-direct character consists in the statutory referendum and the popular initiative applying to constitutional amendments. — cross-ref: S004

chunks.text:
F1. Of the Swiss Protestant (reformed) regions, only Basel and its countryside preserved the Fasnacht through the Reformation. — cross-ref: none
F2. The Basel Fasnacht runs for three days. — cross-ref: none
F3. The Laufenburg town Fasnacht (Städtlefasnacht) is documented since the year 1386. — cross-ref: none
F4. At the third 'Fassel' the Laufenburg Fasnacht deposes the mayor, and the same day features the 'Salm-Alandig'. — cross-ref: none
F5. Solothurn Fasnacht participants nickname their city 'Honolulu' during the carnival season. — cross-ref: none
F6. The 'Naarezumft Honolulu' was founded in 1853 to organise the Solothurn Fasnacht. — cross-ref: none
F7. Solothurn's official carnival start is 13 January ('Hilari'), not 11 November — unlike other carnival traditions. — cross-ref: none
F8. Basel carnival specialities include Mehlsuppe with onion tart (Ziibelewaie) and cheese tart (Chäswaie). — cross-ref: none
F9. The Swabian-Alemannic Fasnet is listed by UNESCO as intangible cultural heritage. — cross-ref: none
F10. Fasnacht traditions now survive in many Swiss cantons. — cross-ref: none

chunks.title: Kanton
chunks.text:
F1. A canton is a member state (Gliedstaat) of the Swiss Confederation; 'Stand' and formerly 'Ort' are alternative historical names for the same unit. — cross-ref: S025
F2. The Helvetic Republic abolished the terms 'Stand' and 'Ort' in 1798 and introduced 'Kanton' as the term for the highest administrative unit. — cross-ref: S037
F3. Cantonal parliaments have between 49 and 180 seats; cantonal governments consist of five or seven members depending on the canton. — cross-ref: S008
F4. The federal government retains a say in many matters that are nominally cantonal competences (the article calls this the 'Kompetänzwirrwarr'). — cross-ref: S025
F5. Allies that were not full members of the Confederacy were called zugewandte Orte (associated places). — cross-ref: S037
F6. Only Glarus and Appenzell Innerrhoden still hold an annual Landsgemeinde in which the citizenry votes by show of hands and elects its cantonal representatives. — cross-ref: S040
F7. Jura is the youngest canton, the 23rd, split off from the canton of Bern in 1979. — cross-ref: S030
F8. The six half-cantons each hold one Council of States seat; the other cantons hold two. — cross-ref: S026
F9. Obwalden and Nidwalden are half-cantons although they were never a single canton. — cross-ref: S026
F10. Uri, Schwyz and Unterwalden are the founding cantons (Urkantön) that concluded the first alliance in 1291. — cross-ref: S037

chunks.text:
F1. The Swiss general strike of 1918 (the Landesstreik) took place from 11 to 14 November 1918. — cross-ref: S037
F2. Over a quarter of a million workers and union members struck in various regions of the country. — cross-ref: none
F3. The Landesstreik is regarded as the most important socio-political confrontation in Swiss early-20th-century history. — cross-ref: none
F4. The Oltener Aktionskomitee was formed in February 1918 and led by National Council member Robert Grimm. — cross-ref: none
F5. On 6 November 1918, out of fear of revolution, the Federal Council called up a massive military contingent. — cross-ref: none
F6. Ultimately some 400,000 workers struck their workplaces. — cross-ref: none
F7. Factories, the public administration, the railways and the newspaper printing works stood still in most Swiss localities. — cross-ref: none
F8. The Federal Council summoned the Federal Assembly to an extraordinary session and demanded an immediate end to the strike. — cross-ref: S002
F9. General Ulrich Wille put Zurich, Bern and other centres under military control under Divisionär Emil Sonderegger. — cross-ref: none
F10. The strike's political effect was the switch from majority to proportional representation in the National Council elections of October 1919. — cross-ref: S003
F11. The new factory act adopted the 48-hour week, and most other demands were subsequently implemented democratically. — cross-ref: S032
F12. The first memorial to the Landesstreik was unveiled in Olten on 11 November 2008, its 90th anniversary. — cross-ref: none

chunks.title: Landsgemeinde
chunks.text:
F1. The Landsgemeinde is one of the oldest and simplest forms of democracy. — cross-ref: S004
F2. In a number of Swiss cantons the Landsgemeinde exists as a cantonal or regional institution, but in most cantons it has been abolished. — cross-ref: S040
F3. Citizens with voting rights assemble on a set day in the open air and vote publicly on the business put to them. — cross-ref: S005
F4. The Landsgemeinde can elect the cantonal government (as in Appenzell Innerrhoden), pass laws or approve the budget. — cross-ref: S008
F5. Voting at the Landsgemeinde is by show of hands, by small sword (Bajonett), or by showing the voting card. — cross-ref: S005
F6. The cantonal Landsgemeinde still exists only in Appenzell Innerrhoden and in the canton of Glarus. — cross-ref: S040
F7. Regional Landsgemeinde still occur in Appenzell Innerrhoden and in the canton of Schwyz; in Graubünden they have not occurred since 2016. — cross-ref: S040
F8. The Landsgemeinde was abolished in Zug and Schwyz in 1848, in Uri in 1928, in Nidwalden in 1996, in Appenzell Ausserrhoden the following year, and in Obwalden in 1998. — cross-ref: S037
F9. The modern Swiss Landsgemeinde resembles the Germanic Thing but derives from the medieval corporations, not from the ancient assembly. — cross-ref: none

chunks.title: Parlament
chunks.text:
F1. Most countries' parliaments have one or two chambers. — cross-ref: S002
F2. In Switzerland the cantonal parliaments do not share a single name: there are Kantonsräte, Grossräte and Landräte. — cross-ref: S008b
F3. In the Old Swiss Confederacy the full assembly of the canton delegates was the Tagsatzung (Diet). — cross-ref: S037
F4. In Swiss German dialect the political assembly word "Daag" (Tag) meant the full body gathered for a political assembly — a dialectal calque still in use for a discussion round ("si tüend daage"). — cross-ref: S037
F5. In the UN the full assembly of the delegates of the member states is the General Assembly — same dialectal root as the Swiss "Daagsatzig". — cross-ref: none
F6. The word "parliament" is also used figuratively today for political assemblies that are not directly representative. — cross-ref: none

F1. Swiss government is strongly decentralised. — cross-ref: S025
